topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Holy Spirit and mission - Peter's Deliverance (Acts 12:8)
question: And the angel said to him, 'Dress yourself and put on your sandal.' The addressee was
explanation: When an angel miraculously rescued Peter from Herod's prison, the angel instructed him, 'Dress yourself and put on your sandals' (Acts 12:8).
proTip: Peter's prison escape is a striking example of angelic intervention in the early church.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - Philip and the Ethiopian (Acts 8:26-38)
question: On the road to Gaza, Philip converted and baptized a
explanation: Led by the Holy Spirit, Philip met an Ethiopian eunuch, a high official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, riding in his chariot on the Gaza road, preached Jesus to him, and baptized him (Acts 8:27-38).
proTip: This event marks an early milestone in the expansion of the Gospel beyond Palestine to Africa.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Conversion of Saul (Acts 9:19-26)
question: After his conversion Paul first went to
explanation: Following his dramatic encounter with Christ on the road to Damascus, Saul spent days with the disciples in Damascus before beginning his ministry there (Acts 9:19).
proTip: Damascus is the immediate site of Paul's conversion, baptism, and early preaching.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Fellowship in the Early Church - Apollos (Acts 18:24)
question: An eloquent Jew from Alexandria, well versed in the Scriptures, was
explanation: Acts 18:24 describes Apollos as a native of Alexandria, an eloquent man well versed in the scriptures, who came to Ephesus and later Corinth.
proTip: Apollos was mentored further in the Christian way by Priscilla and Aquila.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - Jerusalem Council (Acts 15:1-2)
question: The ecumenical Council of 49 A.D. held in Jerusalem was mainly to discuss the
options: fate and requirements of Gentile Christians
explanation: The Jerusalem Council was convened to address whether Gentile converts needed to be circumcised and keep the Mosaic Law to be saved (Acts 15:5, 19-20).
proTip: The Jerusalem Council officially freed Gentile believers from mandatory adherence to Jewish ritual laws.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Paul in Athens (Acts 17:22-23)
question: An altar was set up to the Unknown God in the Greek town of
explanation: When Paul visited Athens, he observed an altar inscribed with the dedication 'To an unknown god,' which he used as a starting point to preach the true Creator God (Acts 17:22-23).
proTip: Athens was famous for its philosophers (Epicureans and Stoics) and numerous idols.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Paul's Appeal (Acts 25:11-12)
question: 'You have appealed to Caesar: To Caesar then you shall go.' This statement was made to Paul by
explanation: When Paul exercised his legal right as a Roman citizen to appeal his case to the Emperor, Governor Festus replied, 'You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you shall go' (Acts 25:12).
proTip: An appeal to Caesar meant Paul had to be transported to Rome for trial.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - Shipwreck at Malta (Acts 28:4)
question: The people of Malta thought that Paul must be a murderer because he
options: was bitten by a poisonous snake
was being taken to Rome as a prisoner
preached to them about the crucifixion of Jesus
was going to answer charges before Caesar.
explanation: When a viper fastened onto Paul's hand after a shipwreck on Malta, the islanders concluded, 'No doubt this man is a murderer. Though he has escaped from the sea, justice has not allowed him to live' (Acts 28:4).
proTip: When Paul suffered no harm from the snake bite, the islanders changed their mind and thought he was a god.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: 'This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman because she was ...'
explanation: According to Genesis 2:23, Adam exclaimed that she shall be called Woman because she was taken out of Man (ishah from ish).
proTip: Notice how Adam recognized the direct ontological connection between himself and the woman.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: When God called Abram out of Haran, his first place of call in Canaan was
explanation: Genesis 12:6 states that Abram passed through the land to the place at Shechem, to the oak of Moreh.
proTip: Shechem was Abraham's very first stopping point and altar site in the Promised Land.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Divine Providence/Guidance - Jacob's Dream at Bethel (Genesis 28:16-17)
question: 'This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven', was said by
explanation: After waking from his dream of the ladder to heaven at Luz, Jacob named the place Bethel, declaring it the house of God and gate of heaven (Genesis 28:16-17).
proTip: Bethel means 'House of God' and marks Jacob's profound spiritual encounter.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The Egyptians enslaved the Israelites and forced them to build
explanation: Exodus 1:11 records that taskmasters were set over the Israelites to afflict them with heavy burdens, and they built for Pharaoh store-cities, Pithom and Raamses.
proTip: Store-cities were built to stockpile provisions and munitions for the Egyptian empire.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The Passover was to remind the Israelites of
options: God's execution of judgment on the gods of Egypt
God's smiting of all the firstborn in Egypt and sparing Israel
The seven days of eating unleavened bread
The eating of roasted lamb while standing.
explanation: The Passover instituted the memorial of God passing over the houses of the Israelites while executing judgment and slaying the firstborn of Egypt (Exodus 12:13, 27).
proTip: The Passover serves as the primary Old Testament type of redemption and deliverance.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The consecration of the people of Israel took place at the foot of Mount
explanation: The entire legal, moral, and ceremonial consecration and covenant-making with Israel took place at the foot of Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:11, 24:4-8).
proTip: Mount Sinai is the sacred mountain where the Law was delivered to Moses.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Obedience and Disobedience - The Golden Calf (Exodus 32:17-18)
question: What occasion is reflected in this statement? 'It is not the sound of shouting for victory, or the sound of the cry of defeat, but the sound of singing that I hear.'
options: Rejoicing for the water from the rock
Praising God after receiving the Ten Commandments
The apostasy of Aaron and the people (Golden Calf revelry).
explanation: When Moses and Joshua descended from Mount Sinai and heard noise in the camp, Joshua mistook it for war, but Moses recognized it as the sound of singing and dancing around the golden calf (Exodus 32:17-18).
proTip: Sin often breaks out rapidly when spiritual leadership is temporarily absent.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: When Moses was instructed to view the Promised Land afar, he
options: summoned the elders and informed them about the land
prayed for a successor to shepherd the people (Numbers 27:15-17).
explanation: When told he would only view Canaan from Mount Nebo, Moses' immediate concern was for the flock, praying to the Lord to appoint a leader over the congregation so they would not be like sheep without a shepherd (Numbers 27:15-17).
proTip: Moses prioritized the future welfare of Israel over his own disappointment.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Who gave this advice? 'Now therefore, fear the Lord and serve him in sincerity and faithfulness; put away the gods which your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.'
explanation: Joshua delivered this famous farewell address and challenge to the assembled tribes of Israel at Shechem, urging them to choose whom they would serve (Joshua 24:14-15).
proTip: Joshua 24:15 ('As for me and my house...') is a cornerstone text for family spiritual leadership.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: To whom was this addressed? 'Rule over us you and your son and your grandson also, for you have delivered us out of the hand of Midian.'
explanation: Impressed by his victory over Midian, the Israelites asked Gideon to establish a hereditary monarchy, which Gideon refused, stating that the Lord would rule over them (Judges 8:22-23).
proTip: Gideon firmly rejected dynastic kingship, recognizing Yahweh as Israel's true King.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Who asked this question? 'Which is better for you—that all seventy of the sons of Jerubbaal rule over you, or that one rule over you?'
explanation: Jotham, the sole surviving son of Gideon, stood on Mount Gerizim and posed this satirical question to the men of Shechem before delivering the fable of the trees (Judges 9:7-15).
proTip: Jotham's fable warned Shechem against the tyranny of Abimelech.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Holiness and Divine Call - Call of Samuel (1 Samuel 3:1-4)
question: At childhood, the word of the Lord came to Samuel because he
options: had the qualities of a prophet
was to announce the punishment for the house of Eli
slept near the ark/lamp of God in the temple.
explanation: 1 Samuel 3:3 notes that Samuel was lying down within the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, when the Lord called him.
proTip: Samuel's proximity to the sanctuary positioned him to receive divine revelation.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Obedience and Disobedience - Saul's Rash Oath (1 Samuel 14:24)
question: 'Cursed be the man who takes food before evening, before I am able to avenge myself on my enemies.' This was said by Saul during the battle between Israel and the
explanation: King Saul imposed a foolish, binding fast upon his exhausted troops during a crucial military engagement against the Philistines at Michmash (1 Samuel 14:24).
proTip: Saul's rash oath nearly caused the execution of his own son, Jonathan, who ate honey.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Davidic Monarchy - Bringing the Ark (2 Samuel 6:6-7)
question: Who was the man who, in an attempt to prevent a disaster, touched the Ark and died when David was returning it to Jerusalem?
explanation: When the oxen stumbled while transporting the ark on a cart, Uzzah put out his hand to steady it and was struck dead by God for irreverence (2 Samuel 6:6-7).
proTip: Uzzah's death highlights the strict holiness required around sacred divine objects.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The suggestion made by prophet Nathan to Bathsheba to foil Adonijah's attempt to usurp the throne of David was to
options: remind David of his promise/oath that Solomon would succeed him
have Solomon secretly anointed by Zadok
plead with Adonijah to abandon the attempt.
explanation: Nathan advised Bathsheba to go into aging King David and remind him of his sworn promise that Solomon their son should reign after him, while Adonijah was staging his coup (1 Kings 1:11-13).
proTip: Nathan acted decisively to ensure Solomon's legitimate succession to David's throne.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Solomon's Reign - Foreign Wives and Idolatry (1 Kings 11:1-4)
question: It was wrong for King Solomon to have married foreign women because
options: they would entice him to worship idols
the women of Israel were more beautiful
a King should not have too many children
explanation: God explicitly warned Israel against marrying foreign nations because they would surely turn away their hearts after their foreign gods, which happened to Solomon in his old age (1 Kings 11:2).
proTip: Solomon's spiritual compromise with foreign idolatry fractured the kingdom's future stability.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile
question: How many months were the Israelites on forced labour in Lebanon allowed to spend at home for every month at the labour camp?
explanation: 1 Kings 5:14 specifies that King Solomon drafted forced labor from all Israel—ten thousand a month in Lebanon by turns; a month they would be in Lebanon and two months at home.
proTip: This heavy corvée labor system contributed greatly to northern resentment against the Davidic crown.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile
subTopic: The Divided Monarchy - Jeroboam's Calf Worship (1 Kings 12:28)
question: Which of the following Kings said 'Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt'?
explanation: Fearing that worship in Jerusalem would cause his subjects to return to Rehoboam, King Jeroboam I made two golden calves and declared this to the northern tribes (1 Kings 12:28).
proTip: Jeroboam's golden calves at Bethel and Dan became the enduring 'sin of Jeroboam' that doomed Israel.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile
subTopic: The Supremacy of God - Elijah and the Widow of Zarephath (1 Kings 17:14)
question: 'The jar of meal shall not be spent and the cruse of oil shall not fail, until the day that the Lord sends rain upon the earth.' From the context, which of these statements is UNTRUE?
options: The meal in the jar and the oil in the cruse were continually replenished thereafter
The widow of Zarephath prepared food for Elijah
The widow and her son ate the food and waited for their death.
The woman was gathering sticks to prepare her last meal
explanation: Option C is untrue because through Elijah's miracle, the jar of meal and cruse of oil did not fail, meaning they did *not* just eat and wait for death, but survived throughout the entire drought period (1 Kings 17:15-16).
proTip: God miraculously sustained Elijah and the widow of Zarephath through supernatural provision during famine.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile
subTopic: The Divided Monarchy - Northern Kings (2 Kings 15)
question: Which of these Kings did not assassinate his predecessor but was assassinated by his successor?
explanation: Pekahiah (son of Menahem) reigned in Samaria and was assassinated in his palace by Pekah (his army captain), who then succeeded him (2 Kings 16:25).
proTip: The late period of the Northern Kingdom was marked by rapid assassinations and political instability.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile
question: Hosea said that the children of Israel shall dwell many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or pillar, without
explanation: Hosea 3:4 prophesies that Israel shall dwell many days without king, prince, sacrifice, pillar, and *without ephod or teraphim*, symbolizing exile and loss of national religious institutions.
proTip: Hosea's prophecy foretold the stripping away of false worship and political autonomy during captivity.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile
subTopic: Religious Reforms in Judah - Manasseh's Evil (2 Kings 21:6)
question: And he burned his son as an offering, and practiced soothsaying and augury, and dealt with mediums and with wizards... To whom does this refer?
explanation: 2 Kings 21:6 describes the extreme wickedness of King Manasseh of Judah, who plunged the nation into horrific occult practices and child sacrifice.
proTip: Manasseh's sins were so grievous that God cited them as the definitive reason for Judah's eventual Babylonian exile.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile
subTopic: Religious Reforms in Judah - Jehoiakim's Reign (2 Kings 23:34)
question: Who was that Egyptian king who not only made Eliakim king of Judah but changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim?
explanation: Pharaoh Neco of Egypt deposed Jehoahaz and made Eliakim the son of Josiah king over Judah and Jerusalem, changing his name to Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:34).
proTip: Pharaoh Neco exercised temporary suzerainty over Judah before the rise of Babylon.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile
subTopic: Concern for Judah - Jeremiah's Letter to Exiles (Jeremiah 29:4-7)
question: Jeremiah wrote to the exiles in Babylon and encouraged them to
options: come back home to rebuild the temple immediately
seek the welfare of Babylon where they were exiled
explanation: Jeremiah instructed the Babylonian exiles to build houses, plant gardens, marry, and seek the welfare of the city where they were sent, because in its welfare they would find their welfare (Jeremiah 29:7).
proTip: Jeremiah counseled peaceful endurance and long-term settlement rather than premature rebellions.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile
question: Which of these prophets made this prophecy of Zion's happy future at the return of the exiles? 'And the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy shall be upon their heads...'
explanation: This magnificent promise of restoration and joyful return to Zion is recorded in Isaiah 35:10.
proTip: Isaiah is known as the evangelical prophet, blending severe warnings of judgment with radiant promises of restoration.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Birth and early life of Jesus - Emmanuel Prophecy (Matthew 1:23)
question: Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel, which means
explanation: Matthew 1:23 quotes Isaiah 7:14, explaining that Emmanuel translated from Hebrew means 'God with us'.
proTip: Emmanuel signifies the incarnation—God dwelling directly among humanity in Jesus Christ.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: What specific reply did John the Baptist give to the soldiers during his preaching?
options: 'Collect no more than is appointed you' (to tax collectors, whereas to soldiers he said 'Rob no one by violence... be content with your wages')
'Do not begin to say to yourselves: we have Abraham as our Father'
'Rob no one by violence or by false accusation, and be content with your wages.'
explanation: When soldiers asked John what they should do, he told them: 'Rob no one by violence or by false accusation, and be content with your wages' (Luke 3:14).
proTip: John gave practical, occupation-specific ethical commands for repentance.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The order of the locations of Jesus' temptations according to Matthew is
explanation: In Matthew's gospel account, the three temptations occur in the wilderness (stones to bread), the pinnacle of the temple, and finally the high mountain (kingdoms of the world) (Matthew 4:1-11).
proTip: Remember Matthew's sequence: Desert $\rightarrow$ Temple $\rightarrow$ Mountain.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: When Christ called Levi to follow Him, he
options: waited two days before he obeyed
accounted for the tax he collected and responded
took some of the money he collected before following Him
left everything, rose, and followed Him.
explanation: Luke 5:28 records that Levi (Matthew) left everything, rose, and followed Jesus immediately.
proTip: Levi's immediate abandonment of his lucrative tax booth illustrates radical discipleship.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The miracle which touched on ingratitude is the
explanation: When Jesus cleansed ten lepers, only one (a Samaritan) returned to give thanks and praise to God, prompting Jesus to ask where the other nine were (Luke 17:17-18).
proTip: The cleansing of the ten lepers underscores the spiritual failing of human ingratitude.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The parable of the unmerciful servant teaches that
options: we should exercise patience until our debtors pay us
we should forgive our debtors from our hearts as God forgave us
debtors should be jailed until they pay all their debts.
explanation: Jesus concluded the parable of the unmerciful servant by stating that His heavenly Father will do the same to every one of us if we do not forgive our brothers from our hearts (Matthew 18:35).
proTip: Divine forgiveness received obligates us to extend heartfelt forgiveness to others.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The ways in which various people hear the word of God are described in the parable of the
explanation: The parable of the sower uses different soil types (path, rocky ground, thorns, good soil) to illustrate human responses to hearing the Word of God (Matthew 13:18-23).
proTip: The sower parable focuses on the condition of the human heart as a receiver of divine truth.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Teachings about Himself - Beelzebub Controversy (Matthew 12:28, Luke 11:20)
question: But if it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out demons, then
options: the kingdom of Satan cannot stand
the kingdom of God has come upon you
the kingdom of Satan is already divided.
explanation: Jesus countered the Pharisees' accusations by stating that if He drove out demons by the finger/Spirit of God, then the Kingdom of God had arrived among them unexpectedly (Matthew 12:28, Luke 11:20).
proTip: Exorcisms performed by Jesus were tangible proofs of the invasion of God's Kingdom.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: 'I assure you, unless you change and become like little children, you will not enter the kingdom of God.' This is a warning by Jesus against
explanation: When the disciples argued about who was greatest in the Kingdom, Jesus called a child to Himself, warning them against self-seeking ambition and pride (Matthew 18:1-4).
proTip: Childlike humility is an indispensable prerequisite for kingdom greatness.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus taught that fasting in addition to prayers is necessary in some situations, during the healing of the
explanation: When the disciples asked why they could not cast out the mute spirit from the epileptic boy, Jesus told them that this kind can come out only by prayer and fasting (Mark 9:29).
proTip: Certain spiritual strongholds require intensified spiritual discipline like prayer and fasting.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus did not grant the request of the sons of Zebedee because
options: they were not qualified for the privilege they asked for
He did not want to encourage rivalry among the disciples
it was not His to grant, except to those for whom it has been prepared by His Father
they could not drink with Jesus' cup.
explanation: Jesus responded to James and John that sitting at His right and left hand was not His to grant, but was for those for whom it had been prepared by His Father (Matthew 20:23, Mark 10:40).
proTip: Divine rewards and positions are sovereignly ordained by the Father.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The parable which teaches persistence in prayer is that of the
explanation: Jesus told the parable of the persistent widow and the unrighteous judge to teach that men ought always to pray and not lose heart (Luke 18:1-8).
proTip: Persistence and importunity in prayer characterize effective petition.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Teachings about Himself - Widow's Mite (Mark 12:41-44, Luke 21:1-4)
question: To give the widow's mite is to give
explanation: Jesus praised the poor widow because out of her poverty she put in all she had to live on, giving more sacrificially than all the rich contributors (Luke 21:3-4).
proTip: God measures giving by the sacrifice involved, not the absolute monetary amount.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Trials and death of Jesus - Crucifixion Witnesses (Mark 15:40, John 19:25)
question: Which of these women was absent during the crucifixion of Jesus Christ according to standard gospel lists?
explanation: Elizabeth (mother of John the Baptist) is never mentioned as being present at the crucifixion of Jesus. The women present included Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James/Joses, Salome, and Jesus' mother Mary.
proTip: Keep track of key women present at the cross across the synoptic and Johannine accounts.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Holy Spirit and mission - Pentecost Prophecy (Acts 2:16-21)
question: To explain the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, Peter quoted Prophet
explanation: In his Pentecost sermon, Peter explained that the dramatic speaking in tongues was the fulfillment of the prophecy spoken by Prophet Joel ('I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh...') (Acts 2:16-21).
proTip: Joel's prophecy is the foundational Old Testament text cited for the Pentecost event.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Fellowship in the Early Church - Ananias and Sapphira (Acts 5:3-4)
question: To whom was this addressed? 'While it remained unsold, did it not remain your own? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How is it that you have contrived this deed in your heart? You have not lied to men but to God.'
explanation: Peter addressed these stern words to Ananias when confronting him about his hypocrisy and deceit regarding the proceeds of his sold land (Acts 5:3-4).
proTip: Ananias and Sapphira faced immediate divine judgment for lying to the Holy Spirit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: 'Truly I perceive that God shows no partiality' was said by
explanation: Realizing through his vision and the outpouring of the Spirit on Cornelius' household that God accepts people from every nation, Peter declared that God shows no partiality (Acts 10:34-35).
proTip: Peter's statement marks the theological breakthrough opening the Gospel fully to Gentiles.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Herod's Persecution (Acts 12:1-3)
question: After the killing of James the son of Zebedee, Herod also arrested Peter because
options: Peter had promised to die with Jesus
the Jews were pleased with the murder of James
Herod wanted to show his zeal for the Law of Moses
Peter was the head of the Church
explanation: Acts 12:3 notes that when King Herod Agrippa saw that the execution of James pleased the Jewish authorities, he proceeded to arrest Peter also during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
proTip: Political expediency often drove civic leaders to persecute early Christian leaders to gain popular favor.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - First Missionary Journey (Acts 13:7)
question: The proconsul of Paphos during the visit of Paul and Barnabas was
explanation: When Paul and Barnabas preached on Cyprus at Paphos, they encountered the intelligent proconsul Sergius Paulus, who desired to hear the word of God and believed (Acts 13:7, 12).
proTip: Sergius Paulus represents an early high-ranking Roman official converted during Paul's journeys.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - Jerusalem Council Envoys (Acts 15:22)
question: Which leading men among the brethren in Jerusalem, and who were themselves prophets, were sent to Antioch with a letter in the company of Paul and Barnabas?
explanation: The Jerusalem church chose two leading men, Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, prominent men among the brethren and prophets, to accompany Paul and Barnabas to Antioch with the council's letter (Acts 15:22, 27).
proTip: Judas Barsabbas and Silas played vital roles in confirming the decree among Gentile believers.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Philippian Jailer (Acts 16:14, 40)
question: Lydia received Paul and Silas into her house when they came to
explanation: Lydia, a dealer in purple goods from Thyatira, had her heart opened by the Lord in Philippi, and she hosted Paul and Silas in her home after her baptism (Acts 16:14-15, 40).
proTip: Lydia was notable as the first recorded European convert to Christianity.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Paul in Athens (Acts 17:22-28)
question: Paul, standing in the Areopagus, used the teaching of the poets of the people to introduce God the Creator at
explanation: While addressing the council of the Areopagus in Athens, Paul quoted Greek poets ('For we are indeed his offspring') to establish common ground for preaching the Creator God (Acts 17:22, 28).
proTip: Paul skillfully bridged pagan philosophy and biblical monotheism in Athens.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - Paul's Journey (Acts 20:4)
question: On his final journey to Jerusalem, Paul lodged at the house of
explanation: Acts 21:16 records that on their final journey toward Jerusalem, disciples accompanied them and brought them to the house of Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple with whom they should lodge.
proTip: Mnason provided hospitality to Paul's traveling missionary entourage.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Paul's Trials (Acts 26:28)
question: 'In a short time you think to make me a Christian' was said by
explanation: When Paul passionately presented the gospel during his defense before King Agrippa, Agrippa remarked, 'In a short time would you persuade me to play the Christian?' (Acts 26:28).
proTip: Agrippa acknowledged the persuasive power of Paul's defense.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - Voyage to Rome (Acts 27:5)
question: The final port of departure for Italy where the Centurion put Paul on board was
options: Myra (where they found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy)
explanation: At the port of Myra in Lycia, the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put Paul and the other prisoners on board (Acts 27:5-6).
proTip: Myra marked the transfer point onto the ill-fated ship bound for Rome.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "Our sister, be the mother of thousands of ten thousands; and may your descendants possess..." Who was the sister?
explanation: When Rebekah left her family to marry Isaac, her family members blessed her with this exact parting wish (Genesis 24:60).
proTip: Rebekah's blessing mirrors the patriarchal promises of immense multiplication.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "Cast out this slave woman with her son; for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac." Who was the slave woman?
explanation: Sarah demanded that Abraham cast out Hagar and her son Ishmael so that Isaac would remain the sole heir (Genesis 21:10).
proTip: Hagar was Sarah's Egyptian maidservant and the mother of Ishmael.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "... thorns and thistles it shall bring forth to you and you shall eat the plants of the field. In the sweat of your face you shall eat bread." To whom were these words spoken?
explanation: God pronounced this judgment and curse upon Adam following human disobedience and the Fall in Eden (Genesis 3:17-19).
proTip: Hard labor and mortality were consequences introduced into human existence through Adam's transgression.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Abraham circumcised his son, Isaac, on the eighth day because
options: It was the custom of his tribe to do so
God commanded him to do so
He wanted to distinguish Isaac from Ishmael
Isaac was the son of promise.
explanation: Abraham strictly obeyed God's specific command to circumcise Isaac on the eighth day as a sign of the everlasting covenant (Genesis 21:4, 17:12).
proTip: Obedience to divine covenant regulations defined the patriarchal walk with God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Who among Joseph's brothers was bound by Joseph when they went to Egypt to buy grain?
explanation: When Joseph tested his brothers during their first journey to Egypt, he took Simeon and bound him before their eyes as a hostage (Genesis 42:24).
proTip: Simeon was kept imprisoned in Egypt until the brothers returned with Benjamin.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Leadership Qualities - Joshua's Division of Land (Joshua 19:49-50)
question: Joshua was buried in the hill-country of
explanation: Joshua was buried in his own inheritance at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of the mountain of Gaash (Joshua 24:30).
proTip: Joshua belonged to the tribe of Ephraim and received his inheritance there.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "Take handfuls of ashes from the kiln and let Moses throw them toward heaven in the sight of Pharaoh." This action resulted in
options: the death of all Egyptian flocks and cattle
the death of the firstborn and beast
boils and sores on man and beast
explanation: When Moses scattered the ashes from the kiln toward heaven as commanded, it became boils breaking out in sores on man and beast throughout Egypt (Exodus 9:8-10).
proTip: The plague of boils marked the failure of the Egyptian magicians even to stand before Moses.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Whoever touches the 'mountain of God' shall be put to death by
explanation: Exodus 19:13 specifies that whoever touches Mount Sinai shall be stoned or shot with an arrow (put to death by shooting or stoning), whether beast or man.
proTip: Strict boundary lines around Sinai emphasized the unapproachable holiness of God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Obedience and Disobedience - The Golden Calf (Exodus 32:2-4)
question: "Take off the rings of gold which are in the ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters, and bring them to me." This was done for
explanation: Aaron demanded these gold earrings from the Israelites to melt them down and fashion a molten calf idol while Moses was on the mountain (Exodus 32:2-4).
proTip: Aaron's compliance with the people led to the grave sin of the golden calf.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: God commanded that Aaron should speak for Moses to the Israelites, but Moses should be to Aaron as
explanation: When Moses hesitated due to his slowness of speech, God appointed Aaron as his spokesman, telling Moses that Aaron would speak for him to the people, and Moses would be to him as God (Exodus 4:16).
proTip: Moses held the ultimate prophetic authority, while Aaron functioned as his mouthpiece.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: On the first day when the Israelites left part of the bread, it bred worms and became foul, but on the sixth day when they left part of the bread it did not become foul because
options: God commanded them to keep it for the Sabbath
Moses wanted to save them the trouble of searching for bread everyday
by them they had discovered a better way of preserving it.
explanation: God commanded the Israelites to keep a double portion of manna on the sixth day for the Sabbath rest, during which none would fall, preserving it miraculously from worms (Exodus 16:23-24).
proTip: The preservation of the Sabbath manna demonstrated divine sanction of the weekly rest.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Who was regarded as the greatest prophet in the Old Testament for seeing God face to face?
explanation: Deuteronomy 34:10 explicitly records that there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face.
proTip: Moses stands unrivaled in traditional Jewish and Christian pneumatology as the supreme lawgiver and prophet of the Old Covenant.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "Whoever rebels against your commandment and disobeys your words, whatever you command him, shall be put to death: only be strong and of good courage." The above passage was addressed to:
explanation: Following the death of Moses, God encouraged Joshua and the people pledged absolute obedience to his leadership under this divine mandate (Joshua 1:16-18).
proTip: Courage and obedience to the Book of the Law were prerequisites for Joshua's success.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Which of these statements did God make to Joshua before the crossing of the Jordan?
options: You shall lead my people with the staff of Moses in your hand
The people of Israel will murmur against you as they did to Moses
This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth
You shall select for yourself men of valour who will cross the Jordan with you.
explanation: God commanded Joshua that the book of the law shall not depart out of his mouth, but he should meditate on it day and night (Joshua 1:8).
proTip: Meditation on God's Word was the secret to Joshua's prosperity and success.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Achan, who took of the devoted things during the fall of Jericho was from the tribe of
explanation: Joshua 7:1 specifies that Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the devoted things.
proTip: Achan's hidden sin at Jericho brought defeat upon Israel at the battle of Ai.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Who among the following people was connected with the war between Israel and King Jabin of Canaan?
explanation: Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, played a decisive role in the defeat of Jabin's army commander, Sisera, during the time of Deborah and Barak (Judges 4:17-21).
proTip: Jael's action sealed Israel's victory over King Jabin of Canaan.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "Alas, my daughter! you have brought me very low, and you have become the cause of great trouble to me; for I have opened my mouth to the Lord, and I cannot take back my vow."
explanation: Judge Jephthah spoke these tragic words to his daughter when she came out to meet him first after his rash vow before battling the Ammonites (Judges 11:35).
proTip: Jephthah's rash vow illustrates the danger of making thoughtless promises to God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Parental Responsibility - Birth of Samuel (1 Samuel 1:3)
question: Elkanah went to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD at Shiloh
explanation: 1 Samuel 1:3 records that Elkanah went up from his city year by year (annually) to worship and to sacrifice to the Lord of hosts at Shiloh.
proTip: Annual pilgrimage to the central sanctuary at Shiloh was a regular practice for devout Israelite families.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Uriah did not wish to go down to his house because
options: Joab would set him in the forefront of the battle
the Ark was in the battlefield
explanation: Uriah honorably refused to go home to comfort his wife while the ark, Israel, and Judah were camping in open fields during wartime (2 Samuel 11:11).
proTip: Uriah's extreme loyalty contrasts sharply with King David's moral failure.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "Then the spirit of the Lord will come mightily upon you, and you shall prophesy with them..."
explanation: Samuel told Saul this sign when anointing him king, predicting that the Spirit of the Lord would rush upon him and transform him into another man (1 Samuel 10:6).
proTip: Saul's early coronation was marked by this profound spiritual empowerment.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The evil spirit that tormented Saul left him whenever he
explanation: Whenever the tormenting spirit from God rushed upon Saul, David took the lyre and played it with his hand, bringing relief so that Saul was refreshed and well (1 Samuel 16:23).
proTip: David's musical skill initially brought him into Saul's royal court.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Saul was made king publicly before the Lord and before all the people of Israel at
explanation: Samuel called the people together to the Lord at Mizpah, where Saul was publicly designated and chosen by lot as king over Israel (1 Samuel 10:17-24).
proTip: Mizpah served as the early gathering and assembly site for national decisions.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Solomon's Reign - Queen of Sheba (1 Kings 10:1-3)
question: When the Queen of Sheba heard Solomon's fame concerning the name of the Lord, she came to test him with her
explanation: The Queen of Sheba came to test Solomon with hard questions to evaluate his legendary divinely-given wisdom (1 Kings 10:1).
proTip: Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hidden from the king that he could not explain.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The greatest of David's domestic problems that seemed to break his heart was the
explanation: Absalom's major rebellion, usurpation of the throne, and open civil war against David caused the king profound heartbreak and forced him into temporary exile (2 Samuel 15:10-14).
proTip: Nathan's prophecy that the sword would never depart from David's house materialized through these domestic tragedies.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Besides the gifts of wisdom, what other gift did the Lord promise to Solomon but with a condition?
explanation: God told Solomon that because he asked for wisdom, He also gave him what he did not ask, both riches and honour, such that no other king would compare, *on condition* that he walked in His ways (1 Kings 3:13-14).
proTip: Solomon's conditional promise required ongoing obedience to secure longevity and sustained favor.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Birth and early life of Jesus - Joseph's Dilemma (Matthew 1:19)
question: When Joseph discovered that his betrothed Mary was with child, he decided to divorce her quietly because
options: Mary was too tender and lovely
the angel warned Joseph not to be harsh on Mary
explanation: Matthew 1:19 explains that Joseph, being a just man and unwilling to put her to shame, resolved to divorce her quietly.
proTip: Joseph's righteousness was displayed through his mercy and compassion toward Mary.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Baptism and temptation - Imprisonment of John (Mark 6:19-20)
question: Though Herod wanted to put John the Baptist to death, he feared the people, because they held him to be a:
explanation: Herod feared John and kept him safe, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and protected him because the crowds regarded John as a true prophet (Mark 6:20).
proTip: Public opinion often constrains corrupt political leaders from executing righteous figures prematurely.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Which of these is NOT included in the instructions given to the disciples during their mission?
explanation: Jesus commissioned the twelve to heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, and cast out demons (Matthew 10:8). Acting as civil judges was never part of their spiritual mandate.
proTip: The early missionary mandate focused strictly on spiritual healing and proclaiming the Kingdom.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus asked his disciples not to disclose their vision of the transfiguration until the
explanation: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them, 'Tell no one the vision, until the Son of man is raised from the dead' (Matthew 17:9).
proTip: Premature disclosure of His glory before His suffering would misunderstand His messianic mission.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: When Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ, Jesus replied that it had been revealed to Peter by
options: the spirit of the living God
explanation: Jesus blessed Simon Peter, declaring, 'Flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven' (Matthew 16:17).
proTip: Spiritual insight into Jesus' true identity originates from divine revelation.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Which of the following prophesied the signs of the end?
explanation: In New Testament apocalyptic teaching and Jesus' Olivet discourse, references to the abomination of desolation and signs of the end explicitly point to the prophecies of Daniel (Matthew 24:15, Daniel 9:27).
proTip: Daniel is recognized as the major Old Testament prophet of apocalyptic timelines.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The parable of the labourers in the vineyard teaches above all God's
explanation: The parable of the workers receiving the same denarius regardless of hours worked illustrates the sovereign generosity and grace of God (Matthew 20:15).
proTip: God's grace surpasses strict human standards of proportional economic reward.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to Jesus, every kingdom divided against itself is
explanation: Jesus countered the Pharisees by stating that every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and no city or house divided against itself will stand (Matthew 12:25).
proTip: Internal division destroys structural integrity and operational power.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus taught that one should make friends quickly with one's
explanation: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus advised: 'Make friends quickly with your accuser, while you are going with him to court...' (Matthew 5:25).
proTip: Prompt reconciliation prevents severe legal and relational penalties.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The Pharisees and Scribes accused the disciples of Jesus of transgressing the tradition of the leaders because they
explanation: The Pharisees and scribes asked Jesus why His disciples did not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but ate with defiled (unwashed) hands (Mark 7:5).
proTip: Jesus criticized the Pharisees for elevating human tradition above divine commandments.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Anointing at Bethany - Waste Complaint (Mark 14:4-5, John 12:4-5)
question: "Why this waste? For this ointment might have been sold for a large sum and given to the poor." The event which led to this saying took place in
explanation: This incident occurred in Bethany at the house of Simon the leper, when Mary anointed Jesus' feet with costly spikenard (Mark 14:3-5, John 12:1-3).
proTip: Bethany was the home of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: At His triumphal entry into Jerusalem, Christ had to sit on an ass because He
explanation: Matthew explicitly notes that this took place to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet: 'Behold, your king is coming to you, humble, and mounted on an ass...' (Matthew 21:4-5).
proTip: Jesus' choice of a donkey demonstrated peaceful, humble kingship rather than military conquest.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: "But Jesus answered them, 'You are wrong, because you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.'" Who was addressed?
explanation: Jesus addressed this rebuke to the Sadducees, who denied the resurrection and tried to trap Him with a trick question about levirate marriage (Matthew 22:23-30).
proTip: Remember that the Sadducees did not believe in resurrection, angels, or spirits.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: "... Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn." This passage is on the parable of the
explanation: This passage is the concluding instruction of the parable of the weeds (tares) sown among the wheat (Matthew 13:30).
proTip: The parable teaches that final judgment and separation of righteous and unrighteous will occur at the close of the age.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall..."
explanation: The fourth beatitude promises that those who hunger and thirst for righteousness shall be satisfied (Matthew 5:6).
proTip: Spiritual hunger for God's righteousness is met with divine satisfaction.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Holy Spirit and mission - Ascension and Promise (Acts 1:4-8)
question: Jesus charged his disciples not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father. This promise was fulfilled when
options: the Holy Spirit filled the disciples on the day of Pentecost
the holy Spirit descended upon Cornelius and all who heard Peter's preaching.
explanation: The promise of the Father—the baptism of the Holy Spirit—was fulfilled on the day of Pentecost when the disciples were filled in Jerusalem (Acts 2:1-4).
proTip: Pentecost marked the birth of the Christian church through the outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Fellowship in the Early Church - Post-Ascension Routine (Acts 1:14)
question: On their return to Jerusalem immediately after the Ascension, the apostles devoted themselves to
explanation: Acts 1:14 records that the apostles returned to Jerusalem and devoted themselves with one accord to prayer, together with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus.
proTip: Apostolic ministry was continually grounded in unified prayer.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: One of the main qualifications of the successor to Judas was that he should be a witness
options: from the time of John the Baptist
during the time of Christ's ministry and death
explanation: Peter stipulated that the replacement must have accompanied them all the time Jesus went in and out among them, starting from John's baptism until His ascension, to become with them a witness of His resurrection (Acts 1:21-22).
proTip: Witness to the bodily resurrection was the core qualification for an apostle.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Holy Spirit and mission - Pentecost Explanation (Acts 2:16)
question: Peter explained that the disciples were not filled with new wine but with the Holy Spirit according to the prophecy of
explanation: Peter defended the disciples against accusations of drunkenness by citing the prophetic words of Joel regarding the last days' outpouring of the Spirit (Acts 2:16).
proTip: Joel's prophecy accounted for the miraculous manifestation of tongues at Pentecost.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Gamaliel's Advice (Acts 5:34-39)
question: Who advised the Sanhedrin to keep away from the apostles and let them alone?
explanation: Gamaliel, a respected Pharisee and teacher of the law, advised the Sanhedrin to leave the apostles alone, reasoning that if their plan was of human origin it would fail, but if of God, they could not overthrow it (Acts 5:34-39).
proTip: Gamaliel's pragmatic wisdom saved the apostles from immediate execution.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Saul's Conversion (Acts 9:1-2)
question: Saul travelled to Damascus in order to
options: obtain letters of authority from the High Priest
arrest those belonging to the Way.
explanation: Saul went to Damascus with letters from the high priest to bind and bring back to Jerusalem any believers of 'the Way' he found (Acts 9:1-2).
proTip: Saul's journey to Damascus was intended for violent persecution, resulting instead in his dramatic conversion.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - Jerusalem Council Debate (Acts 15:1-5)
question: Peter was criticized by the circumcision party in Jerusalem because he
explanation: When Peter returned to Jerusalem, the circumcision party criticized him, saying, 'Why did you go to uncircumcised men and eat with them?' (Acts 11:3).
proTip: Table fellowship with uncircumcised Gentiles shocked traditional Jewish-Christian believers.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - Agabus Prophecy (Acts 11:27-28)
question: Who prophesied a great famine over all the world at Antioch?
explanation: Agabus stood up and prophesied by the Spirit that there would be a great famine over all the world, which took place in the days of Claudius (Acts 11:28).
proTip: Agabus was a prominent prophet in the early church who also later foretold Paul's arrest.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - Cornelius Conversion (Acts 10:44)
question: While Peter was still speaking this, the holy Spirit fell on all who heard the word. Where did this happen?
explanation: This pivotal event occurred at the house of Cornelius the centurion in Caesarea, confirming God's acceptance of the Gentiles (Acts 10:24, 44).
proTip: Caesarea is the Gentile counterpart to Jerusalem's Pentecost.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Opposition to the Gospel - Martyrdom of Stephen (Acts 7:58)
question: Then they cast him out of the city and stoned him; and the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
explanation: This passage describes the martyrdom of Stephen, the first Christian martyr, while Saul approved of his execution (Acts 7:58, 8:1).
proTip: Stephen's martyrdom catalyzed the widespread scattering and expansion of the early church.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and Daughters of Men
question: The reference in Genesis chapter 6 to the union between the 'Sons of God' and the 'Daughters of Men' explains the origin of
explanation: Genesis 6:4 says this union produced the Nephilim, mighty men of renown.
proTip: Know the Nephilim connection to Genesis 6.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: The Patriarchs: Isaac, Rebekah, and Esau/Jacob
question: 'Two nations in Rebekah's womb' refers to the
explanation: The two nations were Israel (Jacob) and Edom (Esau).
proTip: Remember Jacob and Esau's descendants.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Joseph and His Brothers in Egypt
question: Joseph's rough treatment of his brothers was to
options: assure himself that they were not spies
explanation: Joseph tested them to see if they had truly repented of their past actions.
proTip: Joseph's tests were about their character change.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Which of the following BEST describes Abraham's reaction to God's promise of a son by Sarah?
explanation: Abraham laughed with joyful optimism at the promise, given their old age.
proTip: Distinguish Abraham's wonder from Sarah's doubt.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: 'Mahanaim is so called because Jacob saw the angels of God as God's
explanation: Mahanaim means 'two camps' or God's army protecting Jacob.
proTip: Know the meaning of Mahanaim.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "I have sinned this time; the Lord is in the right, and I and my people are in the wrong"; Pharaoh said this after the plague of the
explanation: Pharaoh confessed this during the plague of hail (Exodus 9:27).
proTip: Pharaoh's confessions were temporary.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The request of Moses that Israel should be allowed to go and worship God was interpreted by Pharaoh to mean
explanation: Pharaoh accused Moses of making the people idle from their work.
proTip: Pharaoh's economic motive was to keep slaves working.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The Passover lamb was to be kept until the fourteenth day of the first month when the whole assembly was to kill their lambs
explanation: Exodus 12:6 says the lamb was killed in the evening.
proTip: Remember Passover timing.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: The Exodus: Crossing the Red Sea
question: Pharaoh's horsemen and his army overtook the fleeing Hebrews, encamped by the sea, at
explanation: Exodus 14:2 says they camped at Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea.
proTip: Know the Red Sea crossing location.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The sin of the Israelites that led to the punishment by fiery serpents was
options: trying to stone Caleb and Joshua
explanation: Numbers 21:5-6 says the people spoke against God and Moses, so fiery serpents came.
proTip: Link this to the bronze serpent in John 3.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: The Covenant and Law on Sinai
question: During the confirmation of the covenant, Moses was invited by the Lord along with
explanation: Exodus 24:1 lists Moses, Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu.
proTip: Know the covenant ceremony participants.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "Go into the hills, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves three days, until the pursuers have returned; then afterwards you may go your way". Who gave this advice?
explanation: Rahab hid the Israelite spies and gave them this advice in Jericho.
proTip: Rahab's faith saved her family.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: When Joshua burned Ai, he also put to death the king of Ai, by
explanation: Joshua 8:29 says Joshua hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening.
proTip: Know the punishment of the king of Ai.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: In Jotham's parable of the trees, Abimelech is very much likened to the
explanation: Jotham's parable compares Abimelech to the worthless bramble (Judges 9).
proTip: Bramble represents destructive leadership.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The preservation of the twelve stones by Joshua in Gilgal was to
options: remind Israel of the crossing of River Jordan
indicate that the site was a quarry
explanation: The stones were a memorial so future generations would remember the Jordan crossing.
proTip: Memorials in Joshua teach remembrance.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Samson, as a Nazarite, was required to avoid alcohol,
explanation: Nazarite vows included no shaving and avoiding fermented drink, and Samson's downfall involved women.
proTip: Know the three Nazarite restrictions in Numbers 6.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Which city was captured by Joshua before the disaster at Ai?
explanation: Jericho was conquered first, then Ai was defeated after Achan's sin.
proTip: Know the order: Jericho then Ai.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "I have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and I have utterly destroyed the Amalekites." This declaration was made by
explanation: Saul claimed obedience to Samuel, but he had spared Agag and the best livestock.
proTip: Saul's partial obedience led to his rejection.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: "O Lord of hosts, if thou will... give to thy maidservant a son, then I will give him to the Lord all the days of his life, and no razor shall touch his head." Who said this?
explanation: Hannah made this vow at Shiloh when praying for a son, Samuel.
proTip: Hannah's vow is a model of faith.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Leadership Qualities: Eli and His Sons
question: Eli fell down and died because of the
options: capture of the Ark of Covenant
explanation: Eli died after hearing that the Ark of God had been captured by the Philistines.
proTip: The Ark's capture was Israel's greatest loss.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Obedience and Disobedience: Saul and Samuel
question: "Then Saul fell at once full length upon the ground, filled with fear because of the words of Samuel; and there was no strength in him..." This happened when
options: told Saul that God had rejected him and had chosen David to be king
condemned Saul for offering sacrifice before his arrival
explanation: Saul collapsed in fear when Samuel declared God had rejected him and chosen David.
proTip: This was after the Amalekite campaign.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Ammon's incest with Tamar marks the beginning of
options: the intrigues for succession to the throne
explanation: Amnon's crime against Tamar triggered Absalom's revenge and later rebellion, starting succession intrigues.
proTip: David's family troubles led to political instability.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: As David took to flight from Jerusalem on account of Absalom's conspiracy, he was apprehensive of the role of
explanation: David feared Ahitophel, whose counsel was like God's oracle, had joined Absalom.
proTip: Ahitophel was a key advisor.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: To whom did God promise to give the kingdom after Solomon's heart turned away from the Lord?
explanation: God told Ahijah that He would give ten tribes to Jeroboam because of Solomon's idolatry.
proTip: Jeroboam received the northern kingdom.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: What did Solomon provide for Hiram in exchange for timber of cedar and cypress?
explanation: Solomon supplied Hiram with wheat and food for his household in exchange for timber.
proTip: Solomon traded food for building materials.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Birth and Early Life of Jesus
question: The gift of gold to the infant Jesus indicated his
explanation: Gold symbolized kingship/royal status; frankincense deity; myrrh suffering.
proTip: Know the meaning of the magi's gifts.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Birth and Early Life of Jesus
question: Herod ordered the killing of children when he
options: learnt that a king was born
had been tricked by the wise men
could not see the new baby
searched in vain for the wise men
explanation: Herod was furious after realizing the wise men had tricked him and returned home another way.
proTip: The massacre of innocents followed the magi's deception.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Birth and Early Life of Jesus
question: "And you, O Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you shall come a ruler who will govern my people Israel." This statement fulfills the prophecy of
explanation: Micah 5:2 prophesied that the Messiah would come from Bethlehem.
proTip: Micah is the Bethlehem prophecy.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to Mark, what were the disciples forbidden to take for their journey?
explanation: Mark 6:8 says take nothing except a staff—no bread, no bag, no money.
proTip: Compare with Luke's version of the mission instructions.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: How many days elapsed between Peter's confession and transfiguration?
explanation: Matthew 17:1 and Luke 9:28 say about six (or eight inclusive) days after the confession.
proTip: Six days is the standard answer.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The young man who wanted to know from Jesus what good deed would qualify him for heaven, 'went away sorrowful' because he
options: was uncertain about treasure in heaven
would realize little money from the sale of his goods
explanation: The rich young ruler went away sad because he had many possessions and would not sell them.
proTip: Wealth can be a barrier to discipleship.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: In St. Matthew's record of the ethical teaching of Jesus (chapters 5-7), the most important divine demand that will enable a man inherit the kingdom of God is
explanation: Matthew 7:21 says only those who do the will of the Father will enter the kingdom.
proTip: Obedience to God's will is essential.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The answer "You are the Christ, the son of the living God" was made by Peter in the neighbourhood of
explanation: Peter made this confession at Caesarea Philippi.
proTip: Caesarea Philippi is key for Peter's confession.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: "You shall not tempt the Lord your God." To which temptation did Jesus give this reply?
explanation: Jesus quoted Deuteronomy 6:16 when tempted to jump from the temple pinnacle.
proTip: Match each temptation with Jesus' reply.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Which of these parables teaches about judgement and separation?
explanation: The parable of the Dragnet illustrates final judgment where angels separate wicked from righteous.
proTip: Dragnet = judgment parable.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: "If anyone would be first, he must be last of all and servant of all." What does this saying of Jesus teach?
explanation: Jesus taught that true greatness comes through humility and serving others.
proTip: Servant leadership is a kingdom value.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The appearance of Elijah and Moses at the transfiguration indicates the significance of the
explanation: Moses represents the Law and Elijah the Prophets, both testifying to Jesus.
proTip: Law and Prophets point to Christ.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: One of the illustrations of Jesus on true greatness is
explanation: Jesus used a child to teach that greatness requires childlike humility and trust.
proTip: Childlikeness = humility.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: From which town did Jesus send two of his disciples to make adequate preparation for the last entry into Jerusalem?
explanation: Jesus sent two disciples from Bethphage, near the Mount of Olives, to fetch the colt.
proTip: Bethphage is key for the triumphal entry.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Which religious groups asked Jesus about payment of taxes to Caesar?
explanation: The Pharisees and Herodians teamed up to trap Jesus with the tax question.
proTip: Pharisees and Herodians were unlikely allies.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: When the Pharisees accused Jesus' disciples of plucking heads of grain on the Sabbath, Jesus referred them to what David did during the high priesthood of
explanation: Jesus cited David eating the showbread when Ahimelech was high priest (1 Samuel 21).
proTip: David's example shows mercy over legalism.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: "Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees." This leaven is their
explanation: Matthew 16:12 clarifies that the leaven refers to the false teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
proTip: Leaven = corrupting doctrine.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The three thousand converts on the day of Pentecost devoted themselves to
options: breaking of bread and the prayers
explanation: Acts 2:42 says they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers.
proTip: Know the four pillars of early church life.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Two of the seven deacons are
explanation: Acts 6:5 lists Nicanor and Nicolas among the seven deacons.
proTip: Memorize the seven deacons' names.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to the apostles' speech before the Sanhedrin, the Holy Spirit is given by God to
explanation: Acts 5:32 says the Holy Spirit is given to those who obey God.
proTip: Obedience precedes the Spirit's fullness.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: In his speech concerning the replacement of Judas Iscariot, Peter quoted from
explanation: Peter quoted Psalms 69:25 and 109:8 in Acts 1:20 about Judas's replacement.
proTip: Psalms are often quoted in Acts.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: When Peter escaped from prison during the Passover, the guards were
explanation: Acts 12:19 says Herod examined the guards and ordered them to be put to death after Peter's escape.
proTip: The guards paid with their lives.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: One of the seven Hellenists who preached the gospel in Samaria, and from Azotus to the Syrian capital, Caesarea, was
explanation: Philip the evangelist preached in Samaria and traveled to Caesarea (Acts 8).
proTip: Philip the deacon is not the apostle.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Simon the magician was rebuked by Peter in Samaria because he
options: perverted the minds of the people
opposed the teaching of the apostles
wanted to purchase spiritual power with money
explanation: Simon tried to buy the Holy Spirit with money, and Peter rebuked him (Acts 8:18-20).
proTip: Simony is named after Simon's sin.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The disciples were for the first time called Christians in
explanation: Acts 11:26 says the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.
proTip: Antioch is the birthplace of the term 'Christian'.
